title: Settlement of an Allowed Claim on the Travel Protection Plans
content:
An allowed claim on the Travel Protection Plans is paid at the lower of the amount allowed and the benefit
limit that applies to it, less the deductible that applies to it.

## The limits

Each benefit has its own limit. Cancellation and interruption are shares of the declared trip cost; medical,
evacuation and accident benefits are amounts per insured traveller; and baggage, delay and rental benefits are
amounts per traveller with their own inner ceilings per article or per day. A cancellation limit expressed as a
share is the declared trip cost multiplied by the plan's cancellation share and divided by one hundred, rounded
to two decimal places.

## The deductible

The deductible withheld is the one the benefit names, and where the benefit names none the plan's general
deductible is withheld. The total withheld across all claims on one policy never exceeds the plan's policy
deductible ceiling.

## Benefit consumed across the term

Benefit already paid in this policy term is deducted from the limit before the payment is made, so limits are
consumed across the term rather than restored claim by claim.

## Two further terms

A cancel-for-any-reason claim is paid at the plan's own reimbursement share of the trip cost and never at the
full cancellation share. Payment is made to the policyholder in the currency the premium was paid in, and never
to a third party.

## Worked through on hypothetical figures

A cancellation claim of 9000 is allowed in full on a certificate declaring a trip cost of 7000 under a plan whose
cancellation share is 100 per cent and whose general deductible for each claim is 50. The limit that applies is
7000. The lower of the amount allowed and that limit is 7000, and the deductible of 50 is then taken from it, so
the settlement is 6950. Where the same plan had already paid 1000 of cancellation benefit in the term, the limit
available would be 6000 before the deductible, and the settlement 5950. Where the withholding would come to more
than the settlement, the payment is nothing rather than a debt. These figures are an illustration and not terms
of any plan.
